correctness.rationale: PASS. In G=C_p^3 the proper nontrivial subgroups are PG(2,p) points and lines; two distinct points are nonadjacent, lines form a clique and point-line adjacency is incidence. Degrees p+1 versus (p+1)^2 distinguish vertex types, and incidence automorphisms for prime p are PGL(3,p). A determining set is exactly a vertex subset with trivial pointwise projective stabilizer. For p=2, size-2 stabilizers survive and exactly noncollinear point triples plus dual nonconcurrent line triples form the 56 size-3 bases. For odd p, every triple has an elation/homology or diagonal stabilizer, while four-vertex bases are exactly point frames, dual line frames, triangle+avoiding line, and dual. Their respective counts g/24,g/24,g/6,g/6, g=|PGL(3,p)|=p^3(p^3−1)(p²−1), giving 5g/12. Independent complete enumeration of all 168 PGL(3,2) and 5616 PGL(3,3) actions and every subset of sizes 2,3 or 3,4 respectively exactly corroborated 56 and 2340, including four types, and ruled out lower cardinalities. The unlimited classification uses projective geometry, not finite extrapolation.
residual_risks: Prime fields p only, rank 3; no rank >3 or semilinear non-prime-field extension claimed.

originality.rationale: Best-of-knowledge PASS restricted to the sharp determining number and complete minimum projective point/line-base census. The automorphism group PGL(3,p) is background, from projective collineations and a related previously published subgroup-join graph result; it is not original. Boutin's exact determining-set framework treats Kneser graphs, not this distinct mixed point/line graph. Kayacan–Yaraneri treat graph isomorphism of abelian groups, and Shahsavari–Khosravi provide the automorphism homomorphism and intersection graph structure, not the four base types or 5g/12 count. Semantic Resultary search exposed closely related subgroup-intersection domination claims, none implication-covers pointwise automorphism bases. Equivalent finite projective-geometric base enumerations remain a plausible residual risk.
